description: `hash(key) % N` assigns keys evenly but remaps almost all of them whenever N changes: N/(N + 1) of the keys when one node joins N others.
The hash range bent into a circle; nodes and keys are hashed onto it and a key belongs to the first node clockwise.
A lower-bound binary search for the first position greater than or equal to the key's hash, wrapping to the first position.
A joining node takes only the keys between its predecessor and itself, about 1/(N + 1) of all keys; a leaving node hands only its own keys onward.
Many ring positions per physical node, which even out the arcs, spread a failed node's load and let bigger machines take more keys.
The distinct physical nodes met walking clockwise from a key, used as its owner and replicas.
